steps.title: No one did it
body: Form VII's signature is اِنْ prefixed to the root, giving the shape اِنْفَعَلَ.

Two new words share this pattern: اِنْفَتَحَ ("to open, by itself") and اِنْغَلَقَ ("to close, by itself") — the passive/reflexive counterparts of the already-known فَتَحَ and أَغْلَقَ ("to open/close [something]"): اِنْفَتَحَ الْبَابُ فَجْأَةً, "the door opened suddenly," present tense يَنْفَتِحُ.

Form VII is the odd one out: it never takes a person as its subject. A door اِنْفَتَحَ by itself; a person doesn't. That's exactly why اِنْفَتَحَ/اِنْغَلَقَ pair so naturally with the sentences you already know — فَتَحَ الرَّجُلُ الْبَابَ ("the man opened the door") describes someone doing it, while اِنْفَتَحَ الْبَابُ ("the door opened") describes it just happening, with no one named as the doer.

steps.title: Form VII in one sentence

steps.title: No one did it
steps.prompt: اِنْفَتَحَ الْبَابُ فَجْأَةً — who opened the door?

options.label: No one is named — it just happened
The sentence doesn't say, but someone must have

steps.explanation: Form VII (اِنْفَعَلَ) describes something undergoing an action, not someone performing one — that's the whole point of the pattern, not a gap in the sentence.

steps.title: Spot the pattern
steps.prompt: Both verbs start with اِنْ. Which form is that?
steps.explanation: اِنْفَعَلَ prefixes اِنْ to the root — Form VIII instead infixes a ت after the first root letter, and Form IV prefixes a bare أَ with no ن.

steps.title: Six forms down
steps.message: Form VII — اِنْ prefixed, no human subject. Two more forms to go.
